resources.string: Unofficial companion app. Not affiliated with Spotify AB.
Notification access is a special access setting, not an ordinary app permission. SpotifyQuiet uses it only to read Spotify\'s media notification and active media session while monitoring is on.
No events yet. Start monitoring, then play something in Spotify — the log fills as playback changes.
SpotifyQuiet uses this service only to swipe Spotify out of Recent Apps and reopen it when you explicitly arm the recovery experiment. It never reads or records screen content.

When armed in this mode, SpotifyQuiet may swipe Spotify out of Recent Apps and reopen it within a few seconds after a high-confidence possible ad. The accessibility service only acts on your explicit command, never reads screen content, and can be revoked at any time in system settings. The swipe targets the topmost Recent Apps card (assumed to be Spotify); Android may refuse the background relaunch, so outcomes are logged for verification.

Off by default. When enabled, SpotifyQuiet may reopen Spotify only after a high-confidence possible advertisement, with a 60 second cooldown and at most 5 attempts per session. Android can refuse to start an app from the background, so outcomes must be verified on the device.
Android does not expose a supported API for silently swiping another app out of Recent Apps, so the manual swipe-and-reopen workaround cannot be automated here.
Spotify does not appear to be installed, so recovery actions are unavailable.

Everything stays on this device. SpotifyQuiet makes no network requests, has no account, no analytics and no backend. Only the playback metadata needed for diagnosis is kept, in memory, for as long as the app process lives.
